doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

chapter: Radio, the Jazz Institute and Kenton
title: The Stan Kenton alumni event
summary: Going through the Local 47 directory, he found Kenton alumni and built a huge four-day alumni band event for the radio station.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: because people would get very excited over coming to see an alumni band playing. You know it all started with this big Stan Kenton event. I didn’t even intend for that — I never intended for that to be the case. But when I first moved to Los Angeles to take the job at the radio station I got one of the union directories that published Local 47 union directories and I started going through it just to see who was around, and I couldn’t believe that so many of — they still lived in the area, and the one thread that I noticed was that all the Kenton alumni going back to the first band we around. And it dawned on me that you could like really put together an alumni band of all these musicians and have Pete Rugolo, Lennie Niehaus, Shorty Rogers, Marty Paich, you know Hank Levy — all the writers — Bill Russo, Bill Holman — everybody was still alive. And you could actually have them conduct this alumni band. So we put together a four-day event for the radio station and it was huge. We had this huge attendance beyond what anybody expected. It made a great deal of money for the radio station at the time and it established that idea and it established an audience. So through the years as we continued to do these events, and this kind of goes back to your original question on this, we were able to continue to build a mailing list of people who came to these events. So over the years as this list grew and grew we had people that we knew wanted to attend these multi-day events and we had people that came to the local events and people — and we had a lot of people who would fly in even for the local events. Because, again, they knew they were going to see something that they couldn’t see otherwise. I mean if you want to see this big Stan Kenton thing you pretty much had to come. It’s not going to travel and it’s not going to happen anywhere else. So we would put together things like that.
And it’s not going to be on YouTube just yet, right?

Not yet, there was no such thing. So but see I loved every aspect of that, of — ‘cause that’s what I really love doing. And I did a big radio thing where I did a multi-week history of the Kenton orchestra, interviewed all the musicians that were going to be there. So we built up excitement, got people really excited about this thing that was to come and so on. Yeah back then we didn’t even have a non-local audience. There was no — but I think there was that Kenton newsletter. I had no idea that there was this big almost cultish kind of following for Kenton. I’d never —
